This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. **Fork and clone the repository**\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template.git\n   cd python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n   ```\n\n2. **Create a virtual environment**\n\n   ```bash\n   python -m venv .venv\n   source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   ```\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n   ```\n\n4. **Install pre-commit hooks**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install pre-commit\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Create a feature branch**\n\n   ```bash\n   git checkout -b feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n2. **Make your changes**\n\n   - Write code following the project's style guidelines\n   - Add tests for any new functionality\n   - Update documentation as needed\n\n3. **Run quality checks**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Lint code\n   ruff check .\n\n   # Format code\n   ruff format .\n\n   # Type check\n   mypy src/\n\n   # Check file sizes\n   python scripts/check_file_size.py\n\n   # Run all checks together\n   ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src/ && python scripts/check_file_size.py\n   ```\n\n4. **Run tests**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Run tests\n   pytest\n\n   # Run tests with coverage\n   pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term --cov-report=html\n   ```\n\n   If you changed public APIs or docstrings, build the documentation locally to\n   make sure Sphinx still renders without warnings:\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[docs]\"\n   sphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n   ```\n\n5. **Add a changelog fragment**\n\n   For any user-facing changes, create a changelog fragment:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Create a new changelog fragment (similar to `npx changeset` in JS)\n   scriv create\n   ```\n\n   This will create a new file in `changelog.d/`. Lint the Workflows Themselves\n400\t\n401\t**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.\n402\t\n403\tTwo complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:\n404\t\n405\t- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.\n406\t- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.\n407\t\n408\t```yaml\n409\t- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12\n410\t  with:\n411\t    args: -color\n412\t```\n413\t\n414\t- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.\n415\t- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.\n416\t- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.\n417\t- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.\n418\t\n419\t### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n420\t\n421\t**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n422\t\n423\t```yaml\n424\t- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n425\t```\n426\t\n427\t- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n428\t- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n429\t- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n430\t\n431\t### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n432\t\n433\t**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n434\t\n435\tPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n436\t\n437\t```yaml\n438\trelease-preflight:\n439\t  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n440\t  permissions:\n441\t    contents: read\n442\t    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n443\t  steps:\n444\t    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n445\t    - env:\n446\t        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n447\t      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n448\t\n449\trelease:\n450\t  needs: [release-preflight]\n451\t  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n452\t```\n453\t\n454\t- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n455\t- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n456\t- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n457\t- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACT…URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n458\t- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n459\t- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n460\t\n461\t### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n462\t\n463\t**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n464\t\n465\t```yaml\n466\ton:\n467\t  workflow_dispatch:\n468\t    inputs:\n469\t      bump_type:\n470\t        required: true\n471\t        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n472\t```\n473\t\n474\t- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n475\t- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n476\t- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n477\t- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n478\t- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n479\t- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n480\t- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n481\t\n482\t## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n483\t\n484\tThe templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:\n485\t\n486\t```\n487\tDeveloper Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release\n488\t├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass\n489\t├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump\n490\t└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update\n491\t                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package\n492\t                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)\n493\t                          ├── check-file-line-limits\n494\t                          ├── test-suites\n495\t                          ├── test-execution\n496\t                          ├── validate-docs\n497\t                          └── docker-pr-check\n498\t```\n499\t\n500\tEach layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.\n501\t\n502\t## Getting Started\n503\t\n504\t1. **Choose a template** from the table above matching your language\n505\t2. **Use it as a GitHub template** to create your new repository\n506\t3. **Configure secrets** if needed for publishing (OIDC preferred)\n507\t4. **Start developing** with all best practices pre-configured\n508\t\n509\tThe AI solvers will automatically respect and iterate with all configured checks, producing higher quality output than repositories without CI/CD enforcement.\n510\t\n511\t## Automatic CI/CD Remediation\n512\t\n513\tFor an existing repository, you don't need to apply these practices by hand. The `fix` command automates the whole flow:\n514\t\n515\t```bash\n516\tfix https://github.com/owner/repo --ci-cd\n517\t```\n518\t\n519\tThis command:\n520\t\n521\t1. **Detects the repository's languages** using the GitHub Linguist API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`), ordered by the number of bytes per language.\n522\t2. **Selects the matching CI/CD templates** from the table above, sorted so the template for the most-used language comes first.\n523\t3. **Inspects the latest default-branch run of every active workflow** by enumerating the workflow inventory, reading each workflow's time-ordered runs, and validating `head_branch` locally (GitHub's workflow-specific branch index can lag). This catches a failed required workflow on an earlier commit even when a busy workflow fills GitHub's 1,000-result combined-history window or the latest commit has unrelated passing runs, without permanently reporting a deleted workflow's last failure. If an inventory or per-workflow query fails, it falls back to paginated combined branch history; the exact latest-commit query is used only when branch history has no active runs.\n524\t4. **Creates a remediation issue** that lists the failing runs, the detected languages, the recommended templates, and a link back to this document. The issue is created as a **Bug** (with a `bug` label) and its title and text are taken from the [standard remediation template](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139).\n525\t5. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, which iterates until the fixes are merged. Every option `fix` does not consume itself (for example `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`) is forwarded to `/solve`.\n526\t\n527\t### Why the issue is a Bug, and what it leaves out\n528\t\n529\t`--development-log` replaces the template's retired case-study-folder instruction and collects artifacts under `./dev/log/issues/{issue-id}/pulls/{pull-id}`. `/fix` never emits the retired paragraph, including with `--no-solve` or partial option sets. `--deep-analysis` supplies the timeline, root-cause, debug-output, and upstream-reporting guidance, so `fix` conditionally omits the matching paragraphs instead of delivering them twice.\n530\t\n531\tThat omission is only lossless because `/solve` emits the root-cause wording **only for bug-typed issues** — which is why `fix` creates the issue as a Bug. Issue types are configured per organization and labels per repository, so if the target repository accepts neither, the issue is still created without them.\n532\t\n533\tThe retired paragraph cannot be restored by an option combination; `--development-log` is the only supported collection workflow. The remaining conditional omissions are controlled by `--deep-analysis`.\n534\t\n535\t### Language → Template Mapping\n536\t\n537\tThe command maps detected languages to templates as follows (JavaScript and TypeScript share a single template, and so do C, C++ and CMake):\n538\t\n539\t| Detected Language(s)  | Template                                                         |\n540\t| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |\n541\t| JavaScript/TypeScript | `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |\n542\t| Rust                  | `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |\n543\t| Python                | `link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |\n544\t| Go                    | `link-foundation/go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |\n545\t| C#                    | `link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |\n546\t| Java                  | `link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |\n547\t| C/C++, CMake          | `link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |\n548\t| PHP                   | `link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |\n549\t\n550\tLanguages without a dedicated template (for example Shell or Dockerfile) are listed in the issue for awareness, and the closest matching template is recommended.\n551\t\n552\tUse `--dry-run` to preview the issue without creating it, and `--no-solve` to create the issue without starting `/solve`:\n553\t\n554\t```bash\n555\tfix owner/repo --ci-cd --dry-run\n556\tfix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-solve\n557\t```\n558\t\n559\t## References\n560\t\n561\t- [Code Architecture Principles](https://github.com/link-foundation/code-architecture-principles)\n562\t- [Contributing Guidelines](./CONTRIBUTING.md)\n563\t- [Best Practices](./BEST-PRACTICES.md)"

Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n\nThe templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:\n\n```\nDeveloper Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release\n├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass\n├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump\n└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update\n                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package\n                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)\n                          ├── check-file-line-limits\n                          ├── test-suites\n                          ├── test-execution\n                          ├── validate-docs\n                          └── docker-pr-check\n```\n\nEach layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.\n\n## Getting Started\n\n1. **Choose a template** from the table above matching your language\n2. **Use it as a GitHub template** to create your new repository\n3. **Configure secrets** if needed for publishing (OIDC preferred)\n4. **Start developing** with all best practices pre-configured\n\nThe AI solvers will automatically respect and iterate with all configured checks, producing higher quality output than repositories without CI/CD enforcement.\n\n## Automatic CI/CD Remediation\n\nFor an existing repository, you don't need to apply these practices by hand. The `fix` command automates the whole flow:\n\n```bash\nfix https://github.com/owner/repo --ci-cd\n```\n\nThis command:\n\n1. **Detects the repository's languages** using the GitHub Linguist API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`), ordered by the number of bytes per language.\n2. **Selects the matching CI/CD templates** from the table above, sorted so the template for the most-used language comes first.\n3. **Inspects the latest default-branch run of every active workflow** by enumerating the workflow inventory, reading each workflow's time-ordered runs, and validating `head_branch` locally (GitHub's workflow-specific branch index can lag). This catches a failed required workflow on an earlier commit even when a busy workflow fills GitHub's 1,000-result combined-history window or the latest commit has unrelated passing runs, without permanently reporting a deleted workflow's last failure. If an inventory or per-workflow query fails, it falls back to paginated combined branch history; the exact latest-commit query is used only when branch history has no active runs.\n4. **Creates a remediation issue** that lists the failing runs, the detected languages, the recommended templates, and a link back to this document. The issue is created as a **Bug** (with a `bug` label) and its title and text are taken from the [standard remediation template](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139).\n5. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, which iterates until the fixes are merged. Every option `fix` does not consume itself (for example `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`) is forwarded to `/solve`.\n\n### Why the issue is a Bug, and what it leaves out\n\n`--development-log` replaces the template's retired case-study-folder instruction and collects artifacts under `./dev/log/issues/{issue-id}/pulls/{pull-id}`. `/fix` never emits the retired paragraph, including with `--no-solve` or partial option sets. `--deep-analysis` supplies the timeline, root-cause, debug-output, and upstream-reporting guidance, so `fix` conditionally omits the matching paragraphs instead of delivering them twice.\n\nThat omission is only lossless because `/solve` emits the root-cause wording **only for bug-typed issues** — which is why `fix` creates the issue as a Bug. Issue types are configured per organization and labels per repository, so if the target repository accepts neither, the issue is still created without them.\n\nThe retired paragraph cannot be restored by an option combination; `--development-log` is the only supported collection workflow. The remaining conditional omissions are controlled by `--deep-analysis`.\n\n### Language → Template Mapping\n\nThe command maps detected languages to templates as follows (JavaScript and TypeScript share a single template, and so do C, C++ and CMake):\n\n| Detected Language(s)  | Template                                                         |\n| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| JavaScript/TypeScript | `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |\n| Rust                  | `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |\n| Python                | `link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |\n| Go                    | `link-foundation/go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |\n| C#                    | `link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |\n| Java                  | `link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |\n| C/C++, CMake          | `link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |\n| PHP                   | `link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |\n\nLanguages without a dedicated template (for example Shell or Dockerfile) are listed in the issue for awareness, and the closest matching template is recommended.\n\nUse `--dry-run` to preview the issue without creating it, and `--no-solve` to create the issue without starting `/solve`:\n\n```bash\nfix owner/repo --ci-cd --dry-run\nfix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-solve\n```\n\n## References\n\n- [Code Architecture Principles](https://github.com/link-foundation/code-architecture-principles)\n- [Contributing Guidelines](./CONTRIBUTING.md)\n- [Best Practices](./BEST-PRACTICES.md)",

Concurrency Control\n\n**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:\n\n```yaml\njobs:\n  lint:\n    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated\n    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.\n    concurrency:\n      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint\n      cancel-in-progress: true\n    # ...\n\n  deploy:\n    needs: [lint]\n    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}\n    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this\n    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.\n    concurrency:\n      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main\n      cancel-in-progress: false\n    # ...\n```\n\n### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves\n\n**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.\n\nTwo complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:\n\n- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.\n- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.\n\n```yaml\n- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12\n  with:\n    args: -color\n```\n\n- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.\n- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.\n- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.\n- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.\n\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACT…URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. The message did not say what was wrong or who could fix it.\n- **Root cause.** `scripts/preflight-credentials.sh` mapped 422 to `unknown`. PyPI's mint-token endpoint (`warehouse/oidc/views.py`, `_invalid()`) returns 422 with a JSON body for *every* refusal:\n  - `{\"message\":\"Token request failed\",\"errors\":[{\"code\":...,\"description\":...}]}`\n  - Codes: `invalid-payload`, `not-enabled`, `invalid-token`, `invalid-pending-publisher`, `rate-limited`, `invalid-reuse-token` and `invalid-publisher`.\n  - `invalid-publisher` and `invalid-pending-publisher` are a definite answer: no trusted publisher matches this repository and workflow. That is a verdict, not an unknown (best practices 16 \"Report `unknown`, never a guess\" and 17 \"A policy refusal is a decision\").\n- **Fix (dc38fd4).**\n  - The preflight reads the error code from the body. The two publisher codes become `FAIL`, and the message gives the publisher fields to enter (owner, repository, workflow file, environment).\n  - It probes `GET /pypi/<project>/json` so it can link the right PyPI page: a pending publisher for a new project, or the existing project's publishing settings plus a rename hint, because `my-package` belongs to someone else.\n  - The project name is read from `[project].name`.\n  - The other codes and a 422 without a body stay `unknown`.\n- **Evidence after the fix.** The PR run ([excerpt](ci-logs/pr-cicd-38728238909.txt)) shows the real answer: `FAIL: PyPI refused to mint an upload token (422 invalid-publisher: valid token, but no corresponding publisher (Publisher with matching claims was not found))`, followed by the exact settings. It is a warning on the PR and will be an error on `main` until a maintainer acts (see [requirements.md](requirements.md#r2a-and-r2b-what-a-maintainer-must-do)).\n- **Template.** Same failure on the template's own `main` ([excerpt](ci-logs/template-cicd-38041366369.txt)). A repository admin must enable it: .../settings/security_analysis -> Dependency graph -> Enable.`\n- **Analysis.** This is already the intended behaviour. On pull requests the check warns and skips dependency review; on `main` and on the schedule it fails with the setting to change. No commit can fix it, so there is no code change. It is listed as human action R2b.\n- **Template.** The template runs `dependency-review-action` with no such check, so a generated repository with the graph disabled gets an unexplained failure. Reported upstream.\n\n## F3 (W): mypy `--strict-concatenate is deprecated`\n\n- **Root cause.** `pyproject.toml` set `strict_concatenate = true`. mypy deprecated the option in favour of `extra_checks`, which covers it.\n- **Fix (8b243ac).** `extra_checks = true`. mypy 1.20.2 reports success with no warning, and the PR's lint job shows 0 deprecation lines ([excerpt](ci-logs/pr-cicd-38728238909.txt)).\n- **Template.** Same line. Reported upstream.\n\n## F4 (W): lychee `[WARN] ./**/*.html: No files found for this input source`\n\n- **Root cause.** `links.yml` passed the globs `'./**/*.md' './**/*.html'`, and the repository has no HTML file.\n- **Fix (034d5a3).**\n  - lychee now gets the directory `.` with `--extensions md,html --hidden`, as the JS template does.\n  - `--exclude-path dev/log` keeps collected CI logs out.\n  - Checked with `--dump-inputs`: the same 47 files as before. The PR run checks the same 52 links with no warning ([excerpt](ci-logs/pr-links-38728238822.txt)).\n- **Template.** Already reported as template #106; the fix follows it.\n\n## F5 (W): zizmor `running in offline mode by default` in the pedantic pass\n\n- **Root cause.** The second, pedantic zizmor pass runs `pipx run zizmor` without a token. Since zizmor 1.30 it then falls back to offline mode with a warning and skips the audits that query GitHub. The first pass (zizmor-action) is online, because its `token` input defaults to `github.token`.\n- **Fix (131bc9c).**\n  - The step gets `GH_TOKEN: [REDACTED] github.token }}`; the job token is read-only, with `contents: read`.\n  - Locally the online pass evaluates more (15 ignored instead of 12) and still reports no findings.\n  - The PR run shows no warning ([excerpt](ci-logs/pr-workflows-38728238810.txt)).\n- **Template.** Same step. Reported upstream.\n\n## F6 (FN): change detection ignores `.sh` and `.json`\n\n- **Root cause.** `scripts/detect_code_changes.py` counted `.py .toml .yml .yaml` only. A PR that changed only a pipeline shell script, the medbench sample manifest `src/medbench/data/real_samples.json` or `.secretlintrc.json` skipped lint, tests, build and the changelog check.\n- **Fix (7ad4901).** Add `.sh` and `.json`, with tests. `docs/`, `changelog.d/` and `dev/log/` stay excluded.\n- **Template.** `.sh` is already reported as template #107. `.json` is added to that report as a comment.\n\n## F7 (FN): model tests do not run when files they execute change\n\n- **Root cause.** The `pull_request.paths` filter of `model-tests.yml` lacked three files: `tests/test_medbench_real_data.py` (run by `real-data`), `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` (wraps every step) and `pyproject.toml` (the installed dependencies). A PR that broke any of them merged green without running the model tests (best practice 1: run on *relevant* changes, which includes every file the job executes).\n- **Fix (5373cd2).** Add the three paths. A test derives the list of files from the workflow and from `scripts/medbench-model-run.sh`, so the next file the jobs start to run fails the test until it is added.\n- **Template.** Not applicable: `model-tests.yml` exists only in this repository.\n\n## F8 (W, latent FN): the dist upload only warns when `dist/` is empty\n\n- **Root cause.** The `Upload artifacts` step in `release.yml` used the default `if-no-files-found: warn`. A build that produced nothing would pass, and the failure would surface later, in the publish job, as a download error (best practice 17, \"Write logs where the upload step looks\": an upload that finds nothing warns and passes). Reported upstream.\n\n## F9 (latent FP): a third release cancels the one still waiting\n\n- **Root cause.** Template issue #62 removed `queue: max` from the `main-write` concurrency group because actionlint 1.7.12 rejects the key. GitHub documents it, though: `queue: single` (the default) keeps one pending run and cancels it when the next one arrives; `max` keeps up to 100. So the push release, a manual release and a third writer can cancel a release that was due to run, and it shows as grey.\n- **Fix (136a8b3, 8f67b06).**\n  - `queue: max` on `auto-release` and `manual-release`, both with `cancel-in-progress: false`, because GitHub rejects `max` combined with `true`.\n  - `.github/actionlint.yaml` ignores exactly the message `unexpected key \"queue\" for \"concurrency\" section` until rhysd/actionlint#654 ships, so a plain local `actionlint` agrees with CI. Another unknown concurrency key (tested with `queue-size`) still fails actionlint.\n  - Tests check the key set, that `queue: max` is never combined with a `cancel-in-progress` that could be true, and that the ignore list contains only that message.\n  - The CI/CD Pipeline run on the PR started and passed, so GitHub accepted the syntax.\n- **Template.** Already reported as template #105. Its suggestion puts the ignore in CLI args; the config file is noted there as a simpler variant.\n\n## F10 (W, maintenance): first-party actions one major behind\n\n- **Root cause.** `actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/setup-python@v6` and `actions/cache@v5` while v7, v7 and v6 were current. The workflow uses `build-mode: none`. |\n| `tar ... --warning=no-unknown-keyword` | A tar flag that *suppresses* warnings. |\n| `SKIPPED [40] tests/test_medbench_real_data.py ... set MEDBENCH_NETWORK_TESTS=1` | Network tests are opt-in in the unit test job; `model-tests.yml` runs them with downloads. |\n| `\"result\": \"skipped\"` in `Pipeline Status` | `NEEDS_JSON` of jobs that are skipped by design (release jobs on PRs). |\n\n## Considered and left unchanged\n\n- **Dependabot and the changeset check (template #104).** This repository has no `.github/dependabot.yml` and has never had a Dependabot PR, so the false failure cannot occur here.\n- **zizmor-action v0.7.0 and zizmor 1.31.0.** Both were released on 2026-10-15, the day of this PR. The action's digest table had to be checked against the new CLI first.
